title: CLAY COUNTY SHERIFF
full_story:
On Tuesday, March 10th, at approximately 8:05 am the Clay County Sheriff’s Office was dispatched to the 3000 Block of Ironwood Road in Xenia, for a report of a structure fire.  It was also reported that there was still someone in the residence.

When the deputy arrived, the fire had already been extinguished, and it was determined that no one was in the residence.  The deputy collected evidence at the scene that indicated that the fire had been set intentionally and a suspect was taken into custody.  The suspect was transported to a local hospital and was turned over to medical staff for further treatment.

As a result of the investigation, Clay County State’s Attorney Phillip Givens requested an arrest warrant for Jeffery D. Allen, 56, of Xenia, for the offense of Residential Arson.  Allen was taken into custody by the Sheriff’s Office on Wednesday, and remains incarcerated in the Clay County Jail at the time of this release.

The Sheriff’s Office was assisted by the Xenia and Flora Fire Protection Districts, Illinois State Fire Marshal’s Office, Clay County Ambulance Service, and the Clay County State’s Attorney’s Office.

The charge is merely an accusation, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

title: CLAY CITY SCHOOL BOARD MEETS
full_story:
As Board Chairman Misty Lindeman called the meeting to order, she opened the floor to public comment.  The first to speak was Kennedy Mitchel who told members about the upcoming Junior Prom coming up April 18 at Nostalgia Theater in Flora, with coronation starting at 7:00pm.  The theme for the night is Casino Night and she invited the board to attend.  Next, Clay City Music Teacher Santiago Miranda, who has submitted a letter of resignation, thanked the school district and the whole community for the opportunity to teach music to kids.  He announced that he is leaving this fall to enlist in the United States Marine Corps, where he has been invited to join the Marine Corps Band. He said it was a difficult decision, but felt this is his time to act.  He invited everyone to attend the spring band concert on Tuesday, May 7 at 6:00pm in the old gym.  He added there’s also a concert in Mills Park scheduled for Friday, May 22nd at 6:00pm.  Various members shared they were sorry to see him leave and wished him success in the future.

The board approved the meeting agenda and past meeting minutes and then approved the financial report.  Superintendent John Neubaum said the district is pretty much on track with its finances but did say they will need to amend the budget at the June meeting.  He also commented on the first reimbursement for the district’s participation in the E-Rate program, a federal plan providing discounts to schools and libraries to benefit from affordable telecommunications, internet access, and internal network connections.  Neubaum showed excitement about bringing the program to Clay City and is now seeing the fruit of his effort.

In informational items, Supt. Neubaum stated the district now has 208 students with 45 at the junior high and 75 at the high school.  Concerning the Teacher’s Institute on Friday, he said district staff, teachers and the Clay County Sheriff’s Office participated in dan active shooter drill.  He said those involved did a great job and learned a lot.  There was also a report from an exploratory committee.  Principal Brian Wattles explained the purpose of the meeting was that Cisne had approached Clay City Schools about the possibility of co-oping sports teams.  Wattles said the committee stated they wanted to maintain their current co-op agreement with North Clay Schools and the matter was closed.

Principal Wattles then presented his report and began with the senior class trip to Gulf Shores, Alabama where Clay City Seniors enjoyed their trip to the beach and the fun things they experienced.  Wattles referenced the trip science students took to the Effingham Performance Center to learn about weather and about storm chasers.  Junior high students began lessons about the U.S. Constitution and literature classes are moving into novel studies.  He also noted that IAR testing is next week.  At the high school Leland O’Dell and Johnnie Mooney attended the Wabash Valley Student Recognition Banquet.  Leland O’Dell was also honored as an Illinois State Scholar and Molly Lindeman earned a full-ride scholarship for the theater program at Olney Central College.  In other district events, FFA Week included a staff appreciation breakfast/lunch, Read Across America, Miles of Smiles dental, student council blood drive IAR Testing at the Elementary School, book fair, Illinois State Trooper visit for Driver’s Education, Clay Electric Cooperative visited Driver’s Ed and explained how to react to live power lines and the Kids Heart Challenge in February set a goal of raising $1,500 and ended up raising $1,921.

Chairman Lindeman next asked the board and the visitors for comments on food services.  Some said at the beginning of the school year it was improved, but most of the people at the meeting said they no longer eat the school lunch for a variety of reasons including that the food is cold when served, serving size for adults is the same as for children and there’s little variety.  The board will look at improving the meal that is offered as they want students to have a good meal every day.

The board then moved into closed session.  When they returned to open session, members voted to uphold student discipline as presented.

In new business, the board moved rapidly through a laundry list of agenda items.  The first reading of 2026/27 Student Handbook was completed.  Members approved the renewal of IHSA dues for the 2026/27 school year.  The 8th Grade Class Trip to Six Flags was approved for May 9.  Maternity Leave for Jada Phillips was approved.  Music Teacher Santiago Miranda’s letter of resignation was accepted with regret. The board unanimously approved the resolution authorizing honorable non-reemployment of full- time non-tenured(s) teachers due to lack of proper licensure.  Members then unanimously voted NO on the resolution authorizing non-reemployment of full-time, non-tenured teacher not in the last year of probationary service.  The board then approved the retirement of Steve Holt.  The board also approved the administrative compensation package for the 2026/27 school year.  And the Clay City School Board granted permission for the superintendent to begin work on the FY2027 school year and to authorize spending from July 1. 2026 to the adoption of the budget on September 17, 2026.

title: WVC STUDENTS EARN NATIONAL HONORS
full_story:
Nine students from Wabash Valley College recently traveled to Branson, Missouri, to compete in the 2026 National Professional Agriculture Students (PAS) Conference, earning multiple top finishes in both team and individual events.

WVC agriculture program students competed in four team-based career development events, including Farm Business Management, Beef Specialist, Poultry Specialist and College Bowl.  In addition, six students participated in individual competitions spanning agricultural marketing and communications, agribusiness systems, animal systems, plant systems, agricultural education and employment interview events focused on agronomic services and agricultural sales.

The PAS Conference provides opportunities for students to apply classroom and experiential knowledge in competitive settings while developing career-ready skills in agriculture.  Participants engage in real-world scenarios designed to prepare them for future roles in the industry.

Several WVC students earned national recognition for their performances.

Kelby Ochs of Newton, placed first in Employment Interview Agronomic Systems.  Delaney Williams of Olney earned first place in Career Progress Plant Systems.  The Poultry Specialist team of Victoria Rudolphi, Olney, Cali Bunting, Albion, and Rockell Allen, Flora, also secured a first-place finish.

Individually, Rudolphi earned first place in Poultry, while Bunting placed second, and Allen placed third in the same category.

Students said the experience extended beyond competition, providing meaningful personal and professional growth.

“I learned how important the agricultural community is, not only in my community but across the nation,” said Rockell Allen.  “I was also able to gain experiences that will be valuable towards my future goals.”

Cali Bunting highlighted the team dynamic built during the trip.

“My favorite part of the contest was working together with my fellow team members competing in the poultry competition,” Bunting said.

Aaron Hatfield of Robinson emphasized the connections and memories made at the national level.

“My experience at the national PAS conference was a blast,” Hatfield said.  “Getting the chance to meet new people and compete with my classmates is something I will never forget.”

“We are proud of their hard work and dedication,” the WVC Agriculture program said in a statement.  “These experiences help prepare our students for successful futures in agriculture.”

Back (L to R): Victoria Rudolphi, Ben Scott, Kelby Ochs, Aubrey Lambird

Front (L to R): Cali Bunting, Rockell Allen, Joselyn Kocher, Delaney Williams, Aaron Hatfield

title: NORTH CLAY BOARD
full_story:
The North Clay School Board met Wednesday night and swore in a new member.  Jordan Robey took the oath of office at the beginning of the meeting and took his seat.

The board approved an FCCLA overnight trip April 8th through 10th, a 5th grade trip to the Princeton, Toyota Plant on March 26th; a 1st grade trip to the St. Louis, Aquarium on March 31st, an Enrichment trip to Space Camp in Alabama on March 30th, through April 1st, and a 2nd Grade trip to the St. Louis, Zoo on May 1st.

The board recognized Sylvia Robey, Cody Zimdars, Clara Carroll, and Lane Ruholl for their selection to the Illinois Principals Association Student Recognition Banquet and Haven Cash and Sylvia Robey for being named Illinois State Scholars.

The date of the North Clay High School graduation was set for Sunday, May 17th, in the Clay County State Bank Arena.  The baccalaureate program will be held at 2pm with the graduation ceremony starting at 3pm.  The date of the 8th grade promotion will be Monday, May 18th, at 6:30pm, also in the Clay County State Bank Arena.

The board renewed membership in the IHSA and approved Superintendent Keith Price getting bids for school busses and fuel bids for the next school year.

After a closed session the board hired Meghan Borcherding as Special Education Teacher and approved the letters of resignation of Stacey Blair as High School Head Cheerleading Coach, Chloe Lewis as the High School Girls Basketball Assistant Coach, Josh Zink as Head High School Boys Basketball Coach, and Roy Taylor and volunteer High School Boys Basketball Coach.  The board accepted the letter of intent to retire from Lori Parks, effective at the end of the 2025-2026 school year, and re-hired all non-tenured certified staff for the 2026-2027 school year.

title: OLNEY MAN ARRESTED
full_story:
A Washington Indiana police officer arrested an Olney man on Wednesday afternoon after a vehicle was reported stolen from a gas station. Police said a call came in around 2:07 pm about a vehicle stolen from a gas station on the west side of town.

Within about five minutes, a school resource officer spotted a car matching the description.  The officer said the car then headed north.  A patrol officer caught up to the vehicle, pulled it over and arrested the driver without incident.

Police identified the driver as 39-year-old Justin Ashworth of Olney.

title: SCHOLARSHIPS VOTE
full_story:
Illinois voters overwhelmingly sent a message to Governor JB Pritzker in the March 17th primary election: They want him to opt into the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program.

Residents in all or part of 31 Illinois counties had the opportunity to vote on whether they think the state’s students should benefit from the new program, which allows for donor-provided education money.

A resounding 135,000 Illinoisans, over 63% of the vote total on the question as of Wednesday morning, had registered their support for participating.  In every place in which the non-binding referendum question was on the ballot, a majority favored opting into the program.

In most of those locations the question was: “Should Illinois opt into a federal program that would provide public K-12, private school, and homeschool students with privately donated funds for academic needs, such as tutoring and test preparation, educational therapies for students with disabilities, tuition, books, exam fees or for other specified academic needs?”

While the results do not opt Illinois into the program, they send a strong message to Pritzker that he should do so.

Opting in means Illinois students struggling in reading or math could start receiving extra funding next year for tutoring and other academic services.  The program will give a dollar-for-dollar federal tax credit up to $1,700 each year for donations to non-profit scholarship-granting organizations.

But Illinois students can receive the money only if Pritzker opts the state into the program.  If he ignores voters, taxpayers still can receive the federal tax credit for donating to students in other states.

Illinois voters in the primary made their position clear.  Pritzker should listen and opt into the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program.
